key_insight: A thermal scanning probe can directly write individual perovskite quantum dots with atomic-scale placement control, enabling deterministic single-photon emitters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route to integrate high-performance colloidal quantum emitters with photonic structures, which is a key bottleneck for quantum photonics devices.
method: Use a nanoscale-confined formation volume created by a thermal scanning probe.
Site-selectively synthesize CsPbI3 quantum dots with < 25 nm spatial control.
Tune emitter wavelength and directly couple written dots to photonic cavities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, up to 98% single-photon purity at room temperature, and measured spontaneous-emission enhancement in cavities.
watch_item: The approach still requires precise probe-based writing and materials stability control, which may limit throughput and long-term device reliability.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
